g.text: HARMONIC FUNCTIONS, CONJUGATES & MILNE-THOMSON ENGINE
Laplace 2D Field Equation // Orthogonal Trajectory Networks // Milne-Thomson 30s Reconstruction // Exact Differentials
GATE 2027 TITANS ENGINE
SPEC: ULTRA-HD 4K BLUEPRINT
01. 2D LAPLACE FIELD EQUATION & HARMONIC CONJUGATES
Harmonicity condition // Continuous 2nd partials // Conjugate existence theorem
DEFINITION OF A HARMONIC FUNCTION
A real-valued function ϕ(x,y) is harmonic in domain D iff:
1. Its second-order partial derivatives are continuous in D.
2. It satisfies Laplace's Equation: ∇²ϕ = 0.
∇²u = ∂²u/∂x² + ∂²u/∂y² = 0 (uᵣᵣ + uᵤᵤ = 0)
∇²v = ∂²v/∂x² + ∂²v/∂y² = 0 (vᵣᵣ + vᵤᵤ = 0)
★ The real part u and imaginary part v of EVERY analytic function are harmonic!
HARMONIC CONJUGATE DEFINITION & SENSE
If u(x,y) is harmonic in simply connected D, a harmonic function v(x,y) is called
the "harmonic conjugate of u" iff f(z) = u + iv is analytic.
⚠ DANGEROUS ORDER TRAP (NON-SYMMETRIC!):
• If v is the harmonic conjugate of u, then u is NOT the conjugate of v!
• Instead: The harmonic conjugate of v is -u!
Proof: If f = u + iv is analytic, then -i f = v - iu is analytic, so -u is the imaginary part.
★ GATE Trap: "If v is conj of u, is u conj of v?" NO, answer is -u!
POLAR LAPLACE EQUATION & LOGARITHMIC POTENTIALS
POLAR LAPLACIAN FORMULA
r² ϕᵥᵥ + r ϕᵥ + ϕṤṤ = 0
• Standard radial solution: ϕ(r) = A ln(r) + B
★ u(r,θ) = ln r is harmonic for r > 0; its conjugate is v(r,θ) = θ (since ln z = ln r + iθ)
EXACT DIFFERENTIAL CONJUGATE METHOD
Since v is an exact differential: dv = (∂v/∂x) dx + (∂v/∂y) dy
dv = (-∂u/∂y) dx + (∂u/∂x) dy = M dx + N dy
Exactness condition: ∂M/∂y = -uᵤᵤ = uᵣᵣ = ∂N/∂x (guaranteed by ∇²u = 0!)
v(x,y) = ∫ M dx (treating y as const) + ∫ (terms in N free from x) dy + C
Standard textbook integration recipe when explicit v(x,y) formula is requested.
02. ORTHOGONAL TRAJECTORIES & LEVEL CURVE DUALITY
Geometric orthogonality m₁ · m₂ = -1 // Equipotentials & Streamlines // Engineering applications
PROOF OF ORTHOGONALITY OF LEVEL CURVES
Let Family 1: u(x,y) = c₁ and Family 2: v(x,y) = c₂
Differentiating Family 1: du = uᵣ dx + uᵤ dy = 0 ⇒ m₁ = (dy/dx)₁ = -uᵣ / uᵤ
Differentiating Family 2: dv = vᵣ dx + vᵤ dy = 0 ⇒ m₂ = (dy/dx)₂ = -vᵣ / vᵤ
PRODUCT OF SLOPES USING CR (vᵣ = -uᵤ, vᵤ = uᵣ):
m₁ · m₂ = (-uᵣ / uᵤ) · (-vᵣ / vᵤ) = (-uᵣ / uᵤ) · (uᵤ / uᵣ) = -1
⇒ The curves u(x,y) = c₁ and v(x,y) = c₂ intersect at 90° at every point where f'(z) ≠ 0!
PHYSICAL FIELD CORRESPONDENCE
FLUID DYNAMICS (IRROTATIONAL INCOMPRESSIBLE FLOW)
Complex Potential: W(z) = Φ(x,y) + i Ψ(x,y)
Φ(x,y) = Velocity Potential (lines Φ = c₁ are equipotential)
Ψ(x,y) = Stream Function (fluid flows tangent to streamlines Ψ = c₂)
ELECTROSTATICS & HEAT TRANSFER
Complex Potential: Ω(z) = V(x,y) + i U(x,y)
V(x,y) = Equipotential / Isothermal lines (constant temperature)
U(x,y) = Electric Flux / Heat Flow lines (orthogonal to equipotentials)
CLASSROOM DRILL: FINDING HARMONIC CONJUGATE OF u = x³ - 3xy²
STEP 1: VERIFY HARMONICITY
uᵣ = 3x² - 3y² ⇒ uᵣᵣ = 6x
uᵤ = -6xy ⇒ uᵤᵤ = -6x
uᵣᵣ + uᵤᵤ = 6x + (-6x) = 0 ⇒ SATISFIED (Harmonic)
STEP 2: APPLY CAUCHY-RIEMANN
vᵤ = uᵣ = 3x² - 3y² and vᵣ = -uᵤ = 6xy
STEP 3: INTEGRATE TO RECOVER v(x,y)
Integrate vᵤ w.r.t y: v = 3x²y - y³ + g(x)
Differentiate w.r.t x: vᵣ = 6xy + g'(x)
Match with vᵣ = 6xy ⇒ g'(x) = 0 ⇒ g(x) = C
HARMONIC CONJUGATE: v(x,y) = 3x²y - y³ + C
Reconstructed function: f(z) = (x²-3xy²) + i(3x²y-y³) + iC = z³ + iC
03. MILNE-THOMSON 30-SECOND RECONSTRUCTION ENGINE
Fast algebraic extraction of f(z) directly in terms of z without integrating for v or u
CASE 1: REAL PART u(x,y) IS GIVEN
Since f'(z) = uᵣ + i vᵣ = uᵣ - i uᵤ, substitute x = z, y = 0:
Φ₁(z, 0) = uᵣ(z, 0) and Φ₂(z, 0) = uᵤ(z, 0)
f'(z) = Φ₁(z, 0) - i Φ₂(z, 0)
f(z) = ∫ [Φ₁(z, 0) - i Φ₂(z, 0)] dz + C
SPEED DEMONSTRATION ON u = x³ - 3xy²:
Φ₁(x,y) = 3x²-3y² ⇒ Φ₁(z,0) = 3z² | Φ₂(x,y) = -6xy ⇒ Φ₂(z,0) = 0
f'(z) = 3z² - i(0) = 3z² ⇒ f(z) = ∫ 3z² dz = z³ + C (SOLVED IN 15 SECONDS!)
CASE 2: IMAGINARY PART v(x,y) IS GIVEN
Since f'(z) = vᵤ + i vᵣ, substitute x = z, y = 0:
Ψ₁(z, 0) = vᵤ(z, 0) and Ψ₂(z, 0) = vᵣ(z, 0)
f'(z) = Ψ₁(z, 0) + i Ψ₂(z, 0)
f(z) = ∫ [Ψ₁(z, 0) + i Ψ₂(z, 0)] dz + C
⚠ CRITICAL SIGN WARNING:
When u is given: MINUS SIGN ⇒ f'(z) = Φ₁(z,0) - i Φ₂(z,0)
When v is given: PLUS SIGN ⇒ f'(z) = Ψ₁(z,0) + i Ψ₂(z,0) (Common sign slip!)
ADVANCED MILNE-THOMSON: WHEN LINEAR COMBINATIONS (u - v) OR (u + v) ARE GIVEN
TRANSFORMATION ARCHITECTURE
Let f(z) = u + iv. Multiply by (1 + i):
F(z) = (1 + i) f(z) = (u - v) + i (u + v) = U + i V
Here U = u - v is the real part of the new analytic function F(z)!
Apply standard Case 1 Milne-Thomson to U to find F(z).
Then recover original function: f(z) = F(z) / (1 + i)
POLAR MILNE-THOMSON ENGINE
Given u(r, θ): Substitute r = z, θ = 0 into polar derivative:
Integrate directly with respect to z: f(z) = ∫ f'(z) dz + C
Example: u = r² cos 2θ ⇒ uᵥ = 2r cos 2θ ⇒ uᵥ(z,0) = 2z; uṤ = 0
⇒ f'(z) = 2z ⇒ f(z) = z² + C (Immediate solution!)
04. GATE COMPREHENSIVE HARMONIC DRILL SUITE
Exponential, trigonometric, and rational harmonic conjugates solved to perfection
DRILL 1: u(x,y) = eᵘ cos y
Find harmonic conjugate v(x,y) and entire function f(z).
METHOD A: MILNE-THOMSON SHORTCUT
uᵣ = eᵘ cos y ⇒ Φ₁(z,0) = e᷂ cos(0) = e᷂
uᵤ = -eᵘ sin y ⇒ Φ₂(z,0) = -e᷂ sin(0) = 0
f(z) = ∫ e᷂ dz = e᷂ + C
Expanding f(z) = eᵘ⁺ᵢʸ = eᵘ (cos y + i sin y):
⇒ Harmonic Conjugate: v(x,y) = eᵘ sin y + C
DRILL 2: u(x,y) = 1/2 ln(x² + y²)
Find harmonic conjugate and singular points.
CR INTEGRATION PIPELINE:
uᵣ = x / (x² + y²) and uᵤ = y / (x² + y²)
vᵤ = uᵣ = x / (x² + y²) ⇒ v = tan⁻¹(y/x) + g(x)
vᵣ = -y / (x² + y²) + g'(x). Since vᵣ = -uᵤ = -y/(x²+y²):
g'(x) = 0 ⇒ g(x) = C ⇒ v(x,y) = tan⁻¹(y/x) + C
f(z) = ln|z| + i arg(z) = Ln(z) + C
⚠ Singularity: z = 0 is a branch point! Harmonic conjugate is multivalued!
EXAM DECISION MATRIX: WHICH RECONSTRUCTION METHOD TO USE?
USE MILNE-THOMSON IF:
• Problem asks for f(z) in terms of z.
• Problem asks for f'(z₀) at a specific point.
Time required: 15–30 seconds.
Never compute v(x,y) first!
USE CR INTEGRATION IF:
• Problem explicitly asks for v(x,y).
• Options list v(x,y) formulas.
Integrate vᵤ = uᵣ w.r.t y, differentiate w.r.t x to find g'(x).
Check options by differentiating!
USE OPTION ELIMINATION IF:
• Question has 4 choices for v(x,y).
• Test CR: Does ∂v/∂y = ∂u/∂x? If no, eliminate.
• Test: Does ∂v/∂x = -∂u/∂y? If no, eliminate.
Usually eliminates 3 options in 10s!
